Ladybug screen print

Charley Harper reduces a ladybug to a red half-disc with two black dots, set against a gray ground with stylized grass stems.

Source
Cincinnati Art Museum: Ladybug, 2009.67
Creator
Charley Harper
Made
1959
Style
Mid-century modern (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Playful, precise, natural
Evidence
Based on the Cincinnati Art Museum record. The museum serves only a 600 × 446 px image, below this catalogue’s 800 px threshold for observed evidence, so the observations below are provisional. Not stored.
Reviewed

Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The Cincinnati Art Museum catalogues Ladybug as a color screen print by Charley Harper (American, 1922–2007), dated 1959; composition 32.9 × 47 cm on a 38.7 × 52 cm sheet; Gift of the Estate of Charley Harper; accession number 2009.67. Cincinnati Art Museum.

Harper’s serigraphs grew out of his bird paintings for Ford Times in the 1950s. Charley Harper Art Studio.

Observed

  • From the 600 px museum image: a large red shape, a half-disc with a straight edge, carries two black circles. A small black head with cream eyes sits at its straight edge.
  • Thin black legs and antennae are drawn as straight segments.
  • Tan grass stems and seed heads rise at the left beside a black vertical bar, on a flat gray ground with a few speckled dark patches.

Why it belongs

The insect is built from a circle cut in half and two dots: the reduction to a few flat planes that the style’s rubric names.

The saturated red is an exception to the muted palette, used as a single accent on gray.

Borrow

Reduce a creature to one geometric shape plus two or three details.

Use one saturated accent on a quiet gray or cream ground.

What to review next

  • Find an image of this print or another 1950s Harper serigraph at 800 px or more, and review the observations.
